5. Pool Day & Water Safety

Many photos showed Kiara relaxing poolside on a towel after grooming. She appeared calm and comfortable around the pool.

  • Comfort near water does not prove that she is a strong swimmer.
  • Supervise her continuously around the pool and teach her where the exit/steps are.
  • A canine flotation vest may be useful for actual swimming.
  • Because collars and tags can catch on objects, removing the collar during supervised swimming can be safer.

8. Health & Care Topics Discussed

Long-backed build

Because she appears somewhat long-backed and short-legged, the guidance was to treat her conservatively as if she could have Dachshund-type spinal vulnerability: keep her lean, discourage repeated jumping from beds/couches/vehicles, and consider ramps or steps.

Teeth, ears, coat & nails

  • Small dogs benefit from regular tooth brushing and routine dental checks.
  • Drop ears can retain moisture, so they should be dried after bathing or swimming.
  • Her coat will likely need regular brushing between trims.
  • Nails should be checked regularly, though the photos did not provide a definitive nail-length assessment.

Mammary / abdominal appearance

Some photos showed prominent nipples and loose abdominal skin. Possible explanations discussed included normal anatomy, previous pregnancy/nursing, or hormonal history. The advice was to confirm spay status and reproductive history from shelter records and ask a veterinarian to examine any gland that becomes hard, hot, red, painful, swollen, or produces fluid.

9. Brown Crust Deep in the Ear

You later reported brown crust deep inside one ear. Possible causes discussed included ordinary wax, yeast, bacteria, or ear mites.

  • Do not dig into the ear canal.
  • Clean only the easily visible outer portion using gauze/cotton and a dog-safe ear cleaner.
  • Do not use hydrogen peroxide, alcohol, vinegar, oils, or human ear drops.
  • Keep the ear dry after baths or swimming.
  • Schedule a veterinary ear exam, especially if there is odor, redness, scratching, head shaking, pain, wet discharge, or swelling.
  • Seek urgent care for head tilt, loss of balance, bleeding, severe pain, marked swelling, or sudden hearing changes.
Because Kiara was recently adopted, the suggestion was also to check West Valley Animal Shelter paperwork or contact their clinic to see whether a post-adoption ear issue is covered or discounted.
